newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB, Kirch cancel German digital tv plan.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB, Kirch cancel German digital tv plan.

text.p: Satellite television company British Sky Broadcasting (BSkyB), and Kirch Gruppe, the private German media group, confirmed on Friday they had agreed to cancel a planned deal to create a jointly-owned digital tv platform in Kirch's DF1 company.
The agreement had been terminated "because of failure to agree a number of fundamental issues", the firms said in a joint statement that had been broadly anticipated in the press.
BSkyB, Kirch cancel German digital tv =2

Last July, BSkyB said it was to take a 49 percent stake in DF1, Kirch's German digital television platform, but the talks dragged and six weeks ago the British firm said it was still going through due diligence.
The partnership plan had been complicated by BSkyB's interest in taking a stake in a second German tv venture, Premiere, in which Kirch owns 25 percent.
Kirch has been at loggerheads with partners Bertelsmann AG of Germany and French pay TV group Canal Plus .
Both these two want Premiere, currently an analogue service, to be Germany's main digital television outlet rather than DF1.
BSkyB had appeared poised to take a 25 percent stake in Premiere last year, before switching its focus to DF1.
Australia's News Corp Ltd owns 40 percent of BSkyB.
